_comment: TTS-only respellings for Grades R-3 phonics lines (voice_batch/r3_lines.py). Key: the app's R3Line key (by_key) or an exact line text (by_text); value: what the voice is asked to say instead, so it says the letter SOUND, never the letter NAME. The display text in the pack never changes. Lines rendered from a respelling are ASR-checked against this text and flagged needs_listen in the manifest. Draft: sounds are spelled ah (a as in ant), aw (o as in on), ih (i as in insect), mmm, sss, and a short 'uh' after the stops and v/j/n/w (buh, duh, guh, juh, kuh, nuh, vuh, wuh).

by_key.english_home_language.gradeR.term1.w01_s: Listen. Ah, as in ant. Ah, ah, ant. Afro Ant starts with ah!
Listen for ah at the start. Ah, ah, apple.
Open your mouth wide and say ah.
Which one starts with ah, as in ant?
Say the sound with me. Ah, as in apple!
Which body part starts with ah? Ah, ah.
What is this? It starts with ah.
Does it start with ah? Put ah words in the ah group.
My turn! I will find a word that starts with ah.
You caught me! Nose starts with nuh. Ant starts with ah.
Let's listen together. Ah, ah, ant. Ant starts with ah!
by_key.english_home_language.gradeR.term1.w01_w: Let's write ah. Go round like a ball, then a line down. Ah, ah, ant!
Ah is round, with a little line down the side.
Tap the letter that says ah, as in ant.
This letter says ah. Say the sound!
Trace ah with your finger. Go round, then a line down.
Draw a big ah in the air with your arm. What sound does it make?
My turn! I will write ah.
You caught me! I forgot the line down. That is aw, not ah.
Look together. Round, then a line down. Now it is ah!

Listen for vuh at the start. Vuh, vuh, van.

Listen with your ears. Which one starts with vuh?

Smell the flowers! Which one starts with vuh?
What is this? It starts with vuh.
Does it start with vuh? Put vuh words in the vuh group.

Let's listen together. Vuh, vuh, vuvuzela. That starts with vuh!
by_key.english_home_language.gradeR.term1.w03_w: Let's write vuh. Slide down, then slide up. Like a valley! Vuh, vuh, van.
Vuh has one point at the bottom.
Tap the letter that says vuh, as in van.
This letter says vuh. Say the sound!
Trace vuh with your finger. Slide down, then slide up.
Listen with your ears. Which one starts with vuh?
Look with your eyes. Which one is vuh?
My turn! I will write vuh.
Down, up, down, up. Look, I wrote vuh!
You caught me! That is wuh. Vuh goes down and up only once.
Look together. Down, then up. Just once. That is vuh!

by_key.english_home_language.gradeR.term1.w05_w: Let's write guh for Gogo. Go round, then down and curl like a hook.
Guh has a tail that hangs down and curls.

Look together. Round, then down and curl. That is guh!

Down, up and over. Look, I wrote mmm!

Look together. Up and over, up and over. Two humps make mmm!
